//: Copy to ~/.wb-agent-gateway/config.json and edit. CLI flags and environment variables override these values.
//publicUrl: The URL advertised in OAuth metadata. Set this when you put the gateway behind a tunnel or reverse proxy.
//accessCode: Human approval passphrase shown on the consent screen. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 24
//dataDir: Where the signing key, registered clients and tokens live.

upstream.//baseUrl: The local WorkBuddy/CodeBuddy agent service. null = auto-discover via `codebuddy daemon status`.
upstream.//password: Gateway password from ~/.codebuddy/settings.json. null = read it automatically.
upstream.//autoStart: Spawn and supervise `codebuddy --serve` when nothing is listening.
upstream.//env: Extra environment for the spawned upstream. This is how the agent gets its model credential. CODEBUDDY_AUTH_TOKEN (OAuth) beats apiKeyHelper beats CODEBUDDY_API_KEY. CODEBUDDY_API_KEY also needs CODEBUDDY_INTERNET_ENVIRONMENT: omit for International, or internal / ioa / cloudhosted / selfhosted.

openai.//toolsMode: How to handle OpenAI tools. The agent runs its own tool loop and cannot natively return tool_calls, so: "ignore" drops tools and answers in text (flagging X-WorkBuddy-Tools-Ignored); "reject" returns 400 tools_not_supported so a framework that requires tool_calls fails fast; "translate" bridges the formats - declared schemas go into the prompt as a tool protocol and a structured reply comes back as real tool_calls. Use the /mcp endpoint when the caller must drive the agent's own tools.
openai.//permissionMode: Permission mode for OpenAI jobs that omit workbuddy.permissionMode. An OpenAI request cannot answer a permission prompt, so a prompting mode ends in 409 agent_needs_input. "dontAsk" runs pre-approved and safe actions and denies the rest. One of default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions.
